name: Dirichlet character modulo q

ant_standard_definition.formula: chi: Z -> C is periodic mod q, completely multiplicative, and chi(n)=0 when gcd(n,q)>1

equivalent_forms: group character on (Z/qZ)^x extended by zero

examples.name: principal character
examples.values: 1 on residues coprime to 5 and 0 otherwise

counterexamples.claim: every periodic function is a Dirichlet character
counterexamples.counterexample: a periodic function need not be multiplicative

ant_to_pvg_map.map: nu(n) together with labelled prime coordinates determines n mod q; chi becomes a periodic phase/zero observable on decoded valuation points

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: decode n from the labelled valuation vector, reduce mod q, evaluate chi

loses: without prime labels or integer decoding, residue mod q is generally not recoverable
claim_ceiling: Known character theory and exact PVG evaluation route only.

name: Principal character modulo q

pvg_geometric_object.object: valuation points avoiding every prime axis dividing q

preserves: whether n is a unit mod q
loses: the scalar value does not identify the residue class among units

name: Residue-class indicator by character orthogonality

ant_standard_definition.formula: 1_{n congruent a mod q} = (1/phi(q)) sum_chi conjugate(chi(a)) chi(n), for gcd(a,q)=gcd(n,q)=1

conditions: a and n are units modulo q
sum over all Dirichlet characters modulo q

ant_to_pvg_map.map: project a decoded valuation point onto one reduced residue fiber using the finite character basis

preserves: membership in a reduced residue class
loses: after projection to a scalar indicator, other residue and phase information is discarded
claim_ceiling: Orthogonality identity only; no prime-distribution conclusion.

name: Character orthogonality on the unit group

ant_standard_definition.formula: sum_{a mod q, gcd(a,q)=1} chi(a) conjugate(psi(a)) = phi(q) if chi=psi, else 0

conditions: chi and psi are Dirichlet characters modulo q

pvg_geometric_object.object: orthogonal phase basis on reduced residue fibers

preserves: character coordinates of a unit-residue observable
loses: none when the full character spectrum is retained; partial spectra are lossy

name: Chebyshev psi in an arithmetic progression

ant_standard_definition.formula: psi(x;q,a)=sum_{n<=x, n congruent a mod q} Lambda(n)

equivalent_forms: for reduced a: psi(x;q,a)=(1/phi(q)) sum_chi conjugate(chi(a)) psi(x,chi)

ant_to_pvg_map.map: sum log-axis weights over single-axis prime-power points whose decoded integers lie in the residue fiber a mod q

loses: the scalar sum loses individual prime-power locations and character phases
claim_ceiling: No PNT in arithmetic progressions follows from the finite encoding.

claim: Character orthogonality alone proves equidistribution of primes among reduced residue classes
reason: Orthogonality exactly decomposes residue indicators, but equidistribution requires analytic estimates for twisted prime sums or nonvanishing information for L-functions.

prompt: For q=4 and the nonprincipal real character, evaluate chi(15), chi(6), verify multiplicativity on 3 and 5, and explain why this does not prove prime equidistribution mod 4.
expected_route: finite character algebra does not supply asymptotic estimates
failure_modes: assigning a nonzero value to a nonunit
